## Learning Objectives {.unnumbered}

{{< include ../learning_objectives/0650-containers-docker-compose.qmd >}}

## Docker Compose to launch containers

It can be fiddly and error-prone to type long commands into the terminal,
or a GUI every time you want to launch a container.
Even if you are copying and pasting commands,
it can be difficult to make changes to long commands because you cannot click
to a location to make edits.

A better approach is to use Docker Compose to specify how you want
to launch the container.
This way, all the parts of your command are saved in a file.
This helps document how to run the Docker image,
and it can be version controlled as part of a project.

Docker Compose uses a YAML file, specifically named `docker-compose.yml`,
to record how the container should be launched.
This file can include details such as:

- the Docker image and version to use, or how to build it
- how to mount volumes
- what ports to map
- what environment variables to set

`docker run` commands are interchangeable with the parameters specified
in `docker-compose.yml`;
the compose file makes it easier to manage all the `docker run` parameters.
See this resource that can convert a run command to a compose file:
<https://www.composerize.com/>

Here is the `docker-compose.yml` file of [docker-uv-renv](https://github.com/chendaniely/docker-uv-renv),
the project from [Python and R in one image](0648-containers-uv-renv.qmd):

```{.yaml}
services:
  analysis-env:
    build: .
    image: docker-uv-renv
    ports:
      # 2222 on your computer, 22 in the container.
      # "127.0.0.1:2222:22" stops others on the same Wi-Fi from reaching it.
      - "2222:22"
    volumes:
      - .:/workspace
      # ro: read-only
      - ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub:/root/.ssh/authorized_keys:ro
```

Without Docker Compose, building the image and starting the container
takes these two commands, from the project folder:

```bash
docker build --tag docker-uv-renv .
docker run --detach -p 2222:22 -v "$(pwd):/workspace" -v ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub:/root/.ssh/authorized_keys:ro docker-uv-renv
```

Each part of the `docker run` command is a line of the file:

- `services:` lists the containers the project runs.
  This project has one, which it calls `analysis-env`.
- `build: .` builds the image from the `Dockerfile` in this folder,
  like `docker build .`.
- `image: docker-uv-renv` names the image, like `--tag docker-uv-renv`.
- `ports:` maps port 2222 on your computer to port 22 in the container,
  like `-p 2222:22`.
  Port 22 is where the container's ssh server listens.
  The file uses 2222 on your computer, because your computer may already use 22.
- `volumes:` mounts two things, like the two `-v` options.
  `.:/workspace` mounts the project folder at `/workspace`.
  The second line mounts your ssh public key as the list of keys
  that may log in to the container as `root`,
  and `ro` makes it read-only inside the container.
  The key is the one from [SSH for authentication](0210-ssh-authentication.qmd).

::: {.callout-note title="No ssh key yet?"}
To check that you have the key, list it:

```bash
ls ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub
```

If `ls` says `No such file or directory`,
make a key as in [SSH for authentication](0210-ssh-authentication.qmd):

```bash
ssh-keygen -t ed25519
```

Press Enter to save it in the default place, `~/.ssh/id_ed25519`.
Make the key before you start the container.
If the key is missing when the container starts,
Docker makes a folder at `~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub` instead,
and you cannot log in to the container.
:::

Docker Compose reads the paths in the file itself,
so the same file works on macOS, Linux and Windows,
without the Git Bash `/$(pwd)` change from the earlier chapters.

## Docker Compose commands

Run these from the project folder.
`docker compose build` builds the image.
If you built it in [Python and R in one image](0648-containers-uv-renv.qmd),
Docker reuses every layer:

```bash
docker compose build
```

`docker compose up --detach` starts the container.
`--detach` runs it in the background,
so that you get your terminal back while the ssh server keeps running:

```bash
docker compose up --detach
```

```out
[+] up 2/2
 ✔ Network docker-uv-renv_default          Created                                              0.0s
 ✔ Container docker-uv-renv-analysis-env-1 Started                                              0.2s
```

Docker Compose made a network for the project's containers,
and named the container after the project folder and the service.
`docker compose ps` lists the project's running containers:

```bash
docker compose ps
```

```out
NAME                            IMAGE            COMMAND               SERVICE        CREATED        STATUS                  PORTS
docker-uv-renv-analysis-env-1   docker-uv-renv   "/usr/sbin/sshd -D"   analysis-env   1 second ago   Up Less than a second   0.0.0.0:2222->22/tcp, [::]:2222->22/tcp
```

`docker compose exec` runs a command in the running container.
Run `bash` there to get a terminal in it, in `/workspace`:

```bash
docker compose exec analysis-env bash
```

Then, at the container's prompt:

```bash
pwd
ls
```

```out
/workspace
DESCRIPTION  LICENSE   README.md    docker-compose.yml  renv       reports
Dockerfile   Makefile  _quarto.yml  pyproject.toml      renv.lock  uv.lock
```

`/workspace` shows the project folder, because it is mounted there.
Type `exit` to leave the container, which keeps running.
`docker compose down` stops and removes the container and its network:

```bash
docker compose down
```

```out
[+] down 2/2
 ✔ Container docker-uv-renv-analysis-env-1 Removed                                              0.3s
 ✔ Network docker-uv-renv_default          Removed                                              0.1s
```

## Running a Docker container non-interactively using the Docker Compose

We can also use Docker Compose to run containers non-interactively!
We can do this by specifying that we want to `run` the container (instead of `up`
to launch it interactively).
We use the `--rm` flag with the `run` command to make the container ephemeral
(delete it upon exit).
Then we specify the name of the service from the `docker-compose.yml` file
that we want to run (in our `docker-compose.yml` files
so far, we only have one service,
the environment for running the analysis).
And finally, we add the command we want to run non-interactively using the container
(in the example below, we use `make` to run the data analysis pipeline script).

```bash
docker compose run --rm analysis-env make all
```
